Study in Australia

Highly ranked universities, February and July intakes, and a graduate visa after you finish.

Enquire about Australia Find courses in Australia

At a glance

Main intakes
February, July
Master’s degree
1.5–2 years
Bachelor’s degree
3 years
English tests
IELTS, PTE or TOEFL
Visa
Student visa (subclass 500)

Why students choose Australia

  • Several Australian universities rank among the best in the world.
  • February and July intakes fit well with Indian academic calendars.
  • PTE is widely accepted, which many students find easier to schedule.
  • A graduate visa lets eligible students stay and work after their course.

Popular subjects

  • IT and cyber security
  • Engineering
  • Nursing and health
  • Accounting and business
  • Construction management

Documents you will need

  • Passport
  • Class 10, Class 12 and degree mark sheets and certificates
  • English test score
  • Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from your university
  • Genuine Student statement
  • Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
  • Bank statements or an education loan sanction letter

After you graduate

Eligible graduates can apply for the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) to stay and work after their course.

Visa and work rules change. Your counsellor will confirm what applies on the date you apply.

Universities in Australia

See their courses

  • University of Melbourne

    Melbourne, Victoria

    A Group of Eight university where professional degrees are taught at master’s level.

  • Monash University

    Melbourne, Victoria

    A Group of Eight university in Melbourne, with a campus in Malaysia as well.

  • UNSW Sydney

    Sydney, New South Wales

    A Group of Eight university known for engineering and business.

  • Deakin University

    Melbourne and Geelong, Victoria

    Campuses in Melbourne and Geelong, and the first foreign university to open a campus in India, at GIFT City.

  • RMIT University

    Melbourne, Victoria

    A university of technology and design in central Melbourne, known for practical, industry-linked courses.

  • University of Technology Sydney

    Sydney, New South Wales

    A technology-focused university in the centre of Sydney.

  • University of Wollongong

    Wollongong, New South Wales

    A coastal campus south of Sydney. It also runs a campus in India, at GIFT City.
